item.title: 1.0.0-beta.6
item.description:
The app no longer freezes while a plan is being applied, the core stops leaking a connection every time one closes, and the Safari extension builds and carries the entitlement Safari requires.
### Fixed
- **The app stays responsive while a plan is applied.** Applying a plan held the single database lock for the whole operation, including every call to the browser. One plan covering twenty bookmarks could stall every other screen for minutes. The lock is now held only while the app writes, and a separate guard keeps two plans from writing to the same browser profile at once. - **The core no longer leaks a connection.** Every closed connection left a task and both socket halves behind, because the writer task was awaited before its senders were dropped. A long session accumulated them. - **A queued change is no longer dropped.** When the browser answered `success: false`, the queued mutation was deleted as though it had worked. It now stays queued and is retried. - **The connection banner says why the core stopped.** It showed only the title; the reason is now visible. - **No plaintext copy of encrypted rows is left behind.** The pre-migration backup was kept forever, including the rows migration 3 encrypts. It is now removed once every migration commits, and kept only when one fails. - **The Safari extension builds again.** Packaging assembles the appex with `swiftc` instead of `xcodebuild` on a project that has no `project.pbxproj`, so `package-app.sh` reaches the DMG again, and the bundle carries the sandbox entitlement Safari requires.
### New
- **Every check runs on every push.** CI runs `check-all.sh` on each push and pull request, and packages the app on a tag. - **The Safari extension and the workflow are checked automatically.** `check-all.sh` builds the extension and verifies what Safari needs — the bundle id extends the app's, the principal class is really in the binary, the signature seals `Info.plist`, the sandbox entitlement is present — and rejects a workflow with an unknown runner label, an unpinned action or a missing script.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.5
item.description:
Redirect suggestions from Health Scan can now be reviewed in full and applied to your library, and the Confirm suggestion and Not related buttons respond again.
### New
- **Preview before applying a redirect.** After you confirm suggestions on Health Scan, **Preview & apply** lists every affected bookmark: its title, the URL it has today, the new URL, the browser profile and folder, why the redirect was suggested and what the scan saw, and whether it can be changed. Tick the ones you want, confirm, and see the result for each. **Undo** puts the old URLs back. - **Changes reach Safari through export.** Repairs are made in your Agent Bookworm library; Safari's own bookmark file is never touched. Use **Export HTML** after applying and import that file into Safari. A repair stays in place when the app rescans Safari, and an undone repair stays undone. - **Two counts on Health Scan in the sidebar.** One shows redirect suggestions waiting for you, the other likely-dead links.
### Fixed
- **Confirm suggestion and Not related did nothing.** Confirming saved the redirect but left the card on screen, and any further press failed silently. Cards now disappear once you decide, buttons are disabled while a decision is saved, and errors are shown instead of dropped.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.4
item.description:
Agent Bookworm now updates itself, and the duplicate screen can drop a bookmark from every export in one step.
### New
- **Automatic updates.** Agent Bookworm checks for new versions once a day and installs them for you. Use **Check for Updates…** in the app menu to check now, or turn automatic checks off in Settings. - **Drop all copies of a duplicate.** Each duplicate group has a **Drop all** button next to **Keep selected copies**. It removes every copy of that bookmark from the exported HTML after you confirm. The bookmark stays in your library.
### Fixed
- **One row per browser.** Safari no longer shows up twice in the sidebar after a file import, and Chrome no longer gets a second row when you add another Chrome profile. Existing duplicate rows are merged on first launch, and your library is backed up before that happens. - **Bookmark counts for every browser.** Browser profiles showed "Not connected" and no count. Every profile now shows how many bookmarks it holds. - **"Core Engine Unavailable" after a hiccup.** The app reconnects to its engine on its own instead of showing the banner the moment the connection drops. - **Engine restart loop.** Opening the app while an older engine was still running could restart the engine over and over. That no longer happens. - **No more lost bookmarks when two profiles share a name.** Importing a profile whose name matched another browser's profile could replace that profile's bookmarks. Each profile now keeps its own.
